description: Blocks `git reset --hard` and `git clean` with a real `-f`/`--force` flag (alone or clustered with `-d`/`-x`) — both irreversibly wipe uncommitted/untracked work with no undo. Allows `git checkout -- <file>`/`git restore <file>`, bare/`--mixed`/`--soft` reset, and `git clean -n`/no-force. Deny-by-default: no env-var/inline self-service bypass (removed, Alex tg#6554); RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_BLOCK_RESET_HARD with a written justification asks Telegram via trusted tg-ctl before the additive repo-owner agent_hooks.approval_cmd fallback. NOTE: this hook is ALWAYS ON (no opt-in), so with nothing configured reset --hard/clean -f becomes a hard repo-wide block. Every dangerous segment in a CHAINED command is gated (approving one never waves a later one through), so a single invocation can call approval_cmd/the hatch escalation more than once; an internal 10s AGGREGATE budget across the whole chain (see block_reset_hard._MAIN_LOOP_BUDGET_S) denies with a clear message once that budget is spent, rather than let a legitimately-approved multi-segment command run long enough to hit this descriptor's timeout. timeout_ms 960000 STRICTLY EXCEEDS the helper's 930s worst case (tg-ctl ask's 900s cap plus a 30s cleanup margin) by a 30s headroom, so an unanswered/hung tg-ctl resolves to the hook's own deny BEFORE the bridge hits this descriptor budget — never a bridge timeout that would decide via on_error (block-reset is on_error=closed, so that path already fails safe, but the headroom keeps the deny message clear rather than a generic dispatcher denial). Claude Code settings entries that launch cc_hook_bridge must also set timeout >960s; the CC command-hook default is 600s and will preempt this descriptor. on_error=closed: if the check itself fails, deny rather than let a destructive reset/clean through.
